title: FastAPI persists GraphQL models as files without a database server
description:
Update Gherkin to match the process-first Virtuus decision.

Feature: File-backed local GraphQL storage

  Scenario: Create and read an Item with no database server
    Given a local GraphQL process configured for Virtuus file storage
    And no database server is running
    And no container runtime is required
    When I create an Item through GraphQL
    Then I can read that Item through GraphQL
    And a JSON file on disk contains the Item document

  Scenario: Records survive a FastAPI restart
    Given Items and ScoreResults stored as Virtuus files
    When the FastAPI process restarts
    Then those records are still available through GraphQL

  Scenario: GraphQL contract is unchanged
    Given the same CLI commands used against the Postgres-backed local proxy
    When the store is Virtuus files instead of Postgres
    Then create, get, list, and evaluation writes still work

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
Executable Gherkin is in the private GraphQL proxy feature file on PR https://github.com/AnthusAI/Plexus/pull/612 (base `develop`).

Scenarios that pass:
1. Create and read an Item with no database server (URL unset, `/readyz` 200, disk JSON)
2. Records survive a FastAPI restart (new store instance on the same data directory)
3. Composite Identifier roundtrip persists on disk (`createIdentifier` / `getIdentifier` with `itemId`+`name`)

The original third scenario (list and evaluation writes against Postgres parity) was not a useful duplicate of Item create/get; Identifier composite keys are the non-trivial store path. List and evaluation writes remain the existing GraphQL operations and will be exercised on the evaluate-accuracy path.
